text:
morgan: Quick thread — ran a fresh host-side perf sweep for the new kernel-fingerprint selector + micro-batch window change. Observed a ~35% p99 regression on short chat requests (<=64 tokens) w/ high connection churn. Can folks :eyes: and help triage?

casey: ack. do you have the flame + pprof/trace? rough hypothesis: selector is nudging tiny requests onto a path that forces extra proto parse + smallwrite syscalls.

morgan: posting snippets. full trace in the bucket. small flame excerpt: ```pprof flamegraph --focus=ingress_parse  # output trimmed
ingress_parse  42.3%  kernel_selector::choose
proto::parse    18.9%  ingress_proto::decode_field
writev          9.2%  net::socket::flush_small_writes
tokenizer::run  7.1%  ingest::pretokenize```

maria: hmm writev and proto parse standing out. did the kernel fingerprint add an extra parse pass? I remember the selector needs a lightweight header scan.

morgan: it does a 1-2 byte peek to fingerprint, but I instrumented and it seems to re-run an ownership-checked parse when it routes to host-preparse. so two passes for many requests.

sam: can we avoid the second full parse? maybe the selector can stash a minimal parse result (method/frame length) into the request metadata and short-circuit. or make the selector return a route + preparse token blob.

jun: also noticed HPACK/HTTP2 overhead on grpc lanes when connections are short-lived. a bunch of small frames + repeated headers = CPU + smallwrites. infra-bot showed recent increase in small-writes count per-second.

infra-bot: recent-metrics: small_writes_count +12% over baseline, avg headers/frame CPU up 18%, connection churn up 9%. (collected 1768508000-1768509990)

casey: concrete next steps I propose: 1) add memoized lightweight parse output to kernel selector to avoid reparse; 2) coalesce writev on host egress for small frames (aggregate headers with body for first N ms); 3) try a simd tokenizer build on a canary to shave tokenization cost.

maria: +1. for 2) we can use a small per-connection hold window (2-4ms) to batch small writes. need to check tail latency impact. for 3) I have a simd branch local that shows ~20% tokenization CPU win on synthetic workloads.

sam: can we run an A/B where selector uses memoized parse vs. current? I'll wire a per-route canary flag. If memoized parse removes the second parse we should see p99 drop quickly.

morgan: I've uploaded a comparison trace to gs://redwood-perf/host-ingress/1768509999/compare.html. baseline vs selector-memo. baseline p99=123ms, selector-memo p99=88ms for <=64 tokens.

jun: KV cache note: when selector changes routing the key distribution changed; we saw increased eviction churn on shard 7. that could amplify CPU due to rehydration. logging shows kvcache misses +15% correlated with the period.

casey: good catch. add a short-term mitigation: pin hot prefixes to old shard mapping for 30s during rollout to avoid mass-evict. longer term we should make routing less disruptive to cache key locality.

maria: proposed rollout plan: Phase 0: run selector-memo on 5% traffic + simd-tokenizer off; Phase 1: enable writev coalescing as opt-in on same 5%; Phase 2: simd-tokenizer canary; Phase 3: increase to 25% and monitor p95/p99, kvcache miss rate, small_writes_count.

sam: I'll own Phase 0 canary. monger? (typo: morgan) + tagging signal: p99_small=target, kvcache_miss_delta, small_write_rate.

morgan: thanks — I'll coordinate tests and share perf dashboards. if Phase 0 looks good we'll proceed. leaving the trace and notes in the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-6123.

jun: FYI I already pushed a lightweight mutex-free cache metric probe to staging. will dump histograms after the 5% canary.

casey: one more micro-idea — kernel selector could prefer a variant that preserves input buffer ownership to skip copy-to-owned-buffer in preparse. that avoids memcpy for the common small requests. low effort to prototype.

maria: love it. add that to Phase 1 experiments.

morgan: great work team. action items: @sam Phase0 canary, @maria simd tokenizer benching, @casey implement selector memo + buffer-ownership hint, @jun monitor kvcache histograms. I'll update the ticket with timelines. :thumbsup:

sam: on it. will post results in this thread.

maria: will bench simd on cpu types A,B,C and post csvs.

casey: starting PR for selector memo now (WIP).

morgan: closing loop — thanks all for quick replies. will reopen if the canary shows regressions.
